method: Each accepted image was downloaded to a temp scratchpad with curl -L -A Mozilla/5.0, viewed directly, classified against the rubric using the dossier's description of the structure (12 m dome-shaped white/pale inflatable Hypalon rubber bladder, sited 30-45 m offshore in ~1 m water at low tide, orange marker buoy and tether line, diver-assisted install, seam tore during Dec 2019 install), and cross-checked against the source page's caption/depicts text in the card. Scratch copies were deleted after viewing. The one accepted video was not downloaded; its videos.json entry, manual shot-log transcript (11804314_notes.txt), and the two saved frame files were read/viewed instead.

images.card_depicts: The torn seam in the Airwave inflatable bladder, photographed after it ripped during the December 2019 installation attempt
images.what_i_saw: Underwater close-up: pale/white inflatable bladder material with a visible seam/fold line running through the frame, sandy seabed and a mooring line visible; consistent with a torn seam on the bladder underwater.
images.notes: Matches caption; genuine structure/damage shot, not a beach or unrelated scene.

images.card_depicts: Design/technology graphic of the Airwave device showing how it is meant to build on natural swell using air to create bigger waves
images.note_on_type: This is a computer-generated concept render/diagram of the dome bladder and the swell it is meant to lift, not a photograph of the real installed structure. Classified as structure_visible because it clearly shows the reef's shape/design as built (dome, base on seabed), but flagged: it is illustrative, not photographic evidence that the real Bunbury unit ever looked/worked exactly like this.
images.notes: Card correctly describes it as a design/technology graphic, not a real photo; no discrepancy.

images.card_depicts: Aerial view of Bunbury's Back Beach, the intended installation site, just south of the Bunbury Surf Life Saving Club
images.what_i_saw: Aerial/drone photo of a sandy beach with dark reef-rock/seaweed patches and dune vegetation; no bladder, buoy, diver, or any inflatable structure visible; taken pre-installation (companion June 2019 article, before the December 2019 install attempt).
images.notes: Card already labels this as a site photo (not the structure itself); classification matches the card's own framing. No fix needed, but confirms this image alone cannot serve as evidence of the reef itself and should not become the hero image.

images.card_depicts: Aerial/drone photo of the Airwave bladder in the water off Bunbury Back Beach during the December 2019 installation
images.what_i_saw: Aerial shot of a pale circular submerged dome/bladder in shallow turquoise water with an orange marker buoy and a tether line running to it; matches the ABC video's aerial frame almost exactly (same buoy position and bladder shape).

images.card_depicts: Close-up/photo documenting the torn seam of the Airwave bladder after the December 2019 installation failure
images.what_i_saw: Underwater shot of the pale bladder surface with a raised seam ridge running through the frame and mooring lines visible; consistent with the described seam/tear location, though the tear itself is not sharply resolved in this frame.

images.card_depicts: Waveco's own technical diagram of the Airwave inflatable bladder design intended for Bunbury Back Beach
images.what_i_saw: 3D rendering of a dome-shaped bladder on the seabed with a stylised breaking wave peeling over it, labelled as a design diagram; not a photo of the real site.
images.notes: Card correctly labels this a diagram; no discrepancy.

images_rejected_recheck.notes: Confirmed: this is a Maps web-app URL, not a fetchable image; correctly excluded from accepted images.

videos.title: Dream on hold for Bunbury surfers
videos.evidence: Shot log in 11804314_notes.txt: '00:00-00:08 — Aerial/drone shot over turquoise water off Bunbury Back Beach showing the inflated white Airwave bladder sitting on the seabed, a diver near it, and an orange marker buoy nearby.' Frame 11804314_0005.jpg (viewed) confirms an aerial shot of the pale submerged bladder with buoy and tether line, matching the Airwave-from-Above.jpg image almost exactly. The rest of the 35s clip is a vox-pop with a named surfer reacting to the reef's installation failure, and the video's title/topic (ABC News coverage of the Dec 2019 tear) is squarely about the reef, not incidental beach surfing.
videos.notes: This is NOT one of the two videos Lior flagged as showing surfing-at-the-beach-only; those two (YouTube live-cam and podcast) are already marked 'unavailable'/excluded in videos.json and never entered the accepted card. Only this one ABC video is in the accepted card, and it does show the structure.

Airwave, The World's First Inflatable Surf Reef — Digital Hitmen Podcast [Episode 6]
videos_excluded_confirmed.status_confirmed: unavailable (yt-dlp: video unavailable; thumbnail 404); likely audio-only podcast anyway

frames.what_i_saw: Aerial drone shot with ABC News watermark: pale circular submerged bladder in shallow turquoise water, orange marker buoy just above/right of it, faint tether line visible, a diver's shadow near the bladder edge.
Beachfront interview shot of Camille-Audrey Perron at the Back Beach access point (surf-club mural, 'NO ACCESS BEYOND THIS POINT' sign); no reef structure, water, or bladder visible in frame.
frames.notes: Legitimate as a supporting/context frame (identifies the on-record reaction quoted in R1) but not itself evidence of the reef; should not be used alone or as hero image.

summary.problems_found: None matching Lior's 'surfing at the beach, never the reef' pattern. All 5 structure_visible images and the accepted video genuinely show the bladder/seam/tear or its installation; the one site_context_only image (pre-install aerial of the beach) and one site_context_only frame (interview) are already correctly understood in the card as site/context material, not reef-evidence, so no fix to the card is required. This reef's accepted media set appears clean.
summary.hero_rationale: Clearest, highest-resolution, unambiguous aerial photo of the actual bladder in the water (buoy + tether + dome clearly visible), independently corroborated by the ABC video's near-identical aerial frame (11804314_0005.jpg) — two independent sources agree on the structure's appearance in situ.
